adjudication_records.issue_text: The automatic guard in group_member.hbs resolves against the member item context instead of the group, so the remove link renders even for automatic groups and issues a DELETE that always fails with 422

adjudication.rationale: In `group.hbs` the member list is rendered via `{{each member in members itemView="group-member"}}`, meaning each `group-member` view/template is scoped to an individual member item. In `group_member.hbs`, the guard is `{{#unless automatic}} ... {{/unless}}`, but `automatic` is a group property, not a member property, and nothing in `group-member.js.es6` passes/binds the group’s `automatic` into the item view. As a result `automatic` will resolve as undefined/falsey in the member item context, so the remove link will render even for automatic groups, and clicking it triggers `removeMember` -> `Discourse.Group#removeMember` DELETE, which the server rejects for automatic groups (`can_not_modify_automatic` returns 422).

adjudication_records.issue_text: groups_controller.rb update silently sets group.visible = params[:visible] == "true" unconditionally when the param is absent, unlike other guarded param assignments

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::GroupsController#update, `group.visible = params[:visible] == "true"` is executed unconditionally. If `visible` is omitted from the request, `params[:visible]` is `nil`, so the expression evaluates to `false` and will silently flip `visible` to false on update, unlike the guarded `alias_level` assignment (`if params[:alias_level].present?`). This behavior is directly shown in the diff and can cause unintended data changes when partial updates are sent.

adjudication_records.issue_text: groups_controller.rb add_members silently drops unmatched usernames and still returns success_json; usernames.split(",") also doesn't strip whitespace, so "bob, alice" fails to match " alice"

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::GroupsController#add_members, the code does `usernames.split(",")` and passes each raw token to `User.find_by_username(username)` without stripping whitespace. This means inputs like `"bob, alice"` yield a second token `" alice"`, which will not match an actual username and will be skipped. The loop also ignores any unmatched usernames and still returns `success_json` as long as `group.save` succeeds, so the request can report success while failing to add some intended users.

adjudication_records.issue_text: findMembers() result is ignored in route setupController (fire-and-forget): AJAX failures are silently swallowed with no loading state and no .catch, rendering zero members
groups_controller_spec.rb remove_member test uses xhr :put but the route is delete "members", so it actually routes to add_members and the 422 assertion passes by accident
Stale user_count race: next in admin-group.js.es6 clamps offset against group.get("user_count") which is 0 until first findMembers resolves, so offsets can be computed from outdated data

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce async loading (routes now call `model.findMembers()` without awaiting), and `Discourse.Group` defaults `user_count` to 0. However, the alleged bug in `next` is not verifiable as broken behavior from the diff: when `user_count` is 0, `currentPage`/`totalPages` both return 0 and `showingLast` will be true, so `actions.next` returns early and won’t compute a “wrong” offset. Once `findMembers()` resolves it sets `user_count/offset/limit/members`, so paging state updates. The finding’s claim that offsets are computed from stale/outdated data causing a race is not demonstrated by the code shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: N+1 lookup pattern in add_members: User.find_by_username called per username in a loop, with unbounded request size (no cap on number of usernames) in app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb ~line 68

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, the diff shows `usernames.split(",").each` and inside the loop `User.find_by_username(username)` is called for each username, which is an N-per-input lookup pattern. The diff also shows no validation/cap on the number/length of usernames accepted (`params.require(:usernames)` then `split`), so a large request could cause many DB queries. This is a concrete performance/abuse-risk concern introduced by the change, not a functional correctness break.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unbounded limit parameter on groups members endpoint: params[:limit] has no upper clamp, allowing full materialization and serialization of entire group membership; previous 200 cap for automatic groups was removed (app/controllers/groups_controller.rb ~line 22)

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` is used directly in `.limit(limit)` with no upper bound, so a client can request an arbitrarily large `limit` and cause a very large query and JSON serialization (`members: serialize_data(members, ...)`). However, the finding’s claim that a prior hard 200-cap was “removed” is not strictly supported: the old code used a default of 200 only for automatic groups and did not clamp `params[:limit]` either, and non-automatic groups previously returned all members unpaginated. So the unbounded-limit concern is real and diff-grounded, but it’s more of a hardening/perf issue than a clear newly introduced defect/regression.

adjudication_records.issue_text: OFFSET pagination cost on large groups: limit/offset with order(:username_lower) degrades linearly on deep pages, notable for large automatic groups like 'everyone' (app/controllers/groups_controller.rb members)

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `GroupsController#members` to always paginate via `limit` + `offset` and `order(:username_lower)` (e.g., `members = group.users.order(:username_lower).limit(limit).offset(offset)`), returning `meta` with total/limit/offset. This is not a functional correctness defect, but the finding correctly flags a performance/scalability concern inherent to deep OFFSET pagination on large tables (e.g., large groups like `everyone`), which can become linearly slower as `offset` grows. The issue is grounded in the new pagination implementation introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: group.users.delete(user_id) in remove_member followed by unnecessary group.save — extra work though not a perf defect at scale

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#remove_member`, the diff does `group.users.delete(user_id)` and then conditionally calls `group.save` to decide whether to return success (lines added in `remove_member`). For a typical has_many association, `delete` removes the join row immediately; there are no pending attribute changes on `group` that require `save`, so the extra `group.save` is likely redundant work and could be replaced by checking the delete result or handling exceptions. This is a concrete, diff-grounded inefficiency/clarity issue rather than a correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: Breaking change to public GET /groups/:name/members response shape — previously top-level JSON array of GroupUserSerializer objects, now returns {members: [...], meta: {...}} with no version bump (app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:19-32)

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly changes `GroupsController#members` from `render_serialized(members.to_a, GroupUserSerializer)` (previously a top-level serialized list) to an explicit JSON object `{ members: ..., meta: ... }` (app/controllers/groups_controller.rb). The frontend was updated accordingly (`group.js` now expects `result.members`/`result.meta`), so this isn’t an internal break, but it is a backward-incompatible API response shape change for the public GET endpoint, which is a legitimate review concern even if intentional.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: GET /admin/groups/users route removed with no replacement; external tooling gets 404/405 after upgrade (config/routes.rb:49)

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove the `get "users"` route under the admin groups resource in `config/routes.rb` and replaces it with `put "members"` and `delete "members"` routes (no GET equivalent at the same admin path). The app code is updated to use `/admin/groups/:id/members.json` for membership changes and `/groups/:name/members.json` for listing, so this is not an in-app functional defect, but it is a backward-incompatible API/route change that could break any external client still calling the old `GET /admin/groups/users` endpoint.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: PATCH /admin/groups/:id incremental-membership API (changes[:add]/changes[:delete]) removed; PATCH requests now silently no-op with success while making no membership changes (app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb)

adjudication.rationale: Diff removes PATCH-specific incremental membership handling: the old `update` branched on `request.patch?` and applied `params[:changes][:add]/:delete` (now deleted). The new `update` action (`Admin::GroupsController#update`) ignores `params[:changes]` entirely and will still `group.save` and `render json: success_json` even on PATCH requests, resulting in a silent no-op for clients still using the incremental-membership PATCH API. New membership endpoints (`add_members`/`remove_member`) exist, but PATCH now succeeds without performing requested membership changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: POST /admin/groups payload contract changed from nested group: {name, usernames, visible} to flat name/visible; initial members silently dropped and existing callers get name=nil or errors (app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:22-30)

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change the POST /admin/groups contract: `Admin::GroupsController#create` now reads `params[:name]` and `params[:visible]` (flat params) and no longer reads `params[:group][:name]` / `params[:group][:usernames]` (previous nested payload). It also no longer sets initial members (`group.usernames = ...` was removed), so any callers still sending the old nested payload (or expecting to add members at create-time) will either get validation errors (name becomes `''` when `params[:name]` is missing) or have usernames ignored. However, the accompanying JS and specs were updated to match this new contract, suggesting this is an intentional API change/compatibility concern rather than an accidental defect within this PR.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: PUT /admin/groups/:id payload contract changed; params[:group][:visible] nil check causes visible=false to be written when callers send group: {visible: "true"}, a data-corrupting silent behavior change (app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:31-41)

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change the PUT /admin/groups/:id parameter contract: `update` used to read `payload = params[:group]` and now reads top-level `params[:alias_level]`, `params[:visible]`, `params[:name]`. If an old caller still sends `group: { visible: "true" }`, `params[:visible]` will be nil and `group.visible = params[:visible] == "true"` will set `visible` to false (silent behavior change). However, the finding’s reference to a `params[:group][:visible]` nil-check is inaccurate (that code is removed), and within this PR the JS client was updated to send the new top-level shape (`Group#asJSON`), so this is primarily a backward-compatibility/API-change concern rather than a newly introduced internal defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: Pagination off-by-one in totalPages = floor(user_count / limit) + 1 produces a spurious empty page when user_count is an exact multiple of limit (app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6:8-15)
matched_golden_ids: In the next action, capping the next offset at user_count can produce an empty page (e.g., total equal to limit results in offset == total, showing 2/2 with no members). This can cause confusing UX on the last page.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both comments describe an off-by-one pagination bug that creates an extra/empty last page when user_count is an exact multiple of limit (offset can reach user_count / totalPages overcounts), resulting in a confusing empty page at the end.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: removeMember uses group.users.delete(user_id) without verifying membership, group.save is meaningless for HABTM delete, and there is no atomic/validated membership mutation path — adding nonexistent usernames is silently ignored in add_members (app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:78-88)

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#remove_member`, the diff does `group.users.delete(user_id)` and then checks `group.save` to decide whether to return success (lines shown under `def remove_member`). For a HABTM/has_many :through association, `delete` mutates the join table immediately and is not tied to `group.save`, so the `save` gate is at best redundant and at worst could misreport failure for unrelated validation reasons. Separately, `add_members` (new `def add_members`) skips usernames that don't resolve via `User.find_by_username` with no error/feedback, which is a behavior/design concern but not a verifiable defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: automatic context broken in group_member.hbs itemView — {{#unless automatic}} resolves against member item context instead of admin-group controller, rendering remove link on automatic groups' members, leading to 422 after confirm dialog (app/assets/javascripts/admin/templates/group_member.hbs:1)

adjudication.rationale: In `admin/templates/group.hbs` the members are rendered via `{{each member in members itemView="group-member"}}`, which means the item view/template is driven by the per-item context (the member). In `admin/templates/group_member.hbs`, the conditional `{{#unless automatic}} ... {{/unless}}` is unscoped, so it will resolve against the member context, not the parent group/controller. Since a member object won’t have an `automatic` property, `automatic` will be falsy/undefined and the `unless` block will render, showing the remove link even for automatic groups. Clicking it triggers `removeMember` -> `/admin/groups/:id/members.json` DELETE, which the backend rejects for automatic groups (422 via `can_not_modify_automatic`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: No error handling on any client-side AJAX call in group.js, admin-group.js.es6, admin_group_route.js, group-members.js.es6 — missing .catch/failure handlers cause silent promise rejections, stale data, and no user feedback on server errors (P1)

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows multiple new/changed client-side async flows that invoke `Discourse.ajax(...).then(...)` without any explicit failure handling (e.g., `findMembers`, `addMembers`, `removeMember`, `create`, `save` in `group.js`). Also, both `admin_group_route.js` and `group-members.js.es6` now call `model.findMembers();` without returning/handling the promise, so request failures won’t be surfaced or coordinated with route loading/error states. While this may be mitigated by global AJAX error handling elsewhere (not shown), the finding is diff-grounded as a robustness/UX concern rather than a strictly provable defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unhandled rejection in save in admin-group.js.es6 — disableSave set true with no .catch/.finally, leaving save button permanently disabled and no error shown if group.save()/create() fails (P1)

adjudication.rationale: The diff only shows `save` changing from `saveWithUsernames/createWithUsernames` to `save/create` and does not show the rest of the `save` action (where `disableSave` would be set/reset and where `.catch/.finally` might exist). From the visible code we cannot verify that `disableSave` is set to `true` without being cleared, nor that promise rejections are unhandled or that no error is shown on failure.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Paginated fetch race condition in admin-group.js.es6 next/previous — no cancellation/serialization of in-flight findMembers() requests allows out-of-order responses to overwrite newer state, corrupting displayed page and offset (P2)

adjudication.rationale: In `admin-group.js.es6`, `next`/`previous` update `group.offset` and immediately call `group.findMembers()` without any request serialization/cancellation. In `discourse/models/group.js`, `findMembers()` issues an async `Discourse.ajax(...)` and on resolution unconditionally `setProperties({ user_count, limit, offset, members })` from the response. If a user triggers multiple page changes quickly, earlier (slower) requests can resolve after later ones and overwrite `members`/`offset` with stale data, producing an incorrect displayed page/state. The diff contains no guard (e.g., request token, abort, or ignoring stale responses).

adjudication_records.issue_text: add_members in admin/groups_controller.rb silently ignores nonexistent usernames — typo'd or whitespace-padded usernames are dropped without error while endpoint returns success_json (P2)

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, usernames are split on commas and looked up with `User.find_by_username(username)`; any username that doesn’t resolve (including whitespace-padded ones, since no `strip` is applied) is silently skipped, and the action still renders `success_json` as long as `group.save` succeeds. This is a real, diff-grounded API/UX concern (no error reporting/validation for bad input), but the diff doesn’t establish that this behavior is incorrect—similar “silent success” behavior existed previously (e.g., old incremental add tests for non-existent users), so it’s not clearly a defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: remove_member spec uses wrong HTTP verb (xhr :put instead of delete), so the test does not exercise the real route and leaves the automatic-group guard untested (P3)
matched_golden_ids: The remove_member test uses xhr :put to call the remove_member action, but the route defines delete 'members' => 'groups#remove_member' requiring DELETE method.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags that the remove_member spec uses the wrong HTTP verb (PUT via xhr) and should use DELETE to match the route, which is the same underlying issue described in the golden comment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unbounded limit parameter on public members endpoint in groups_controller.rb — no upper clamp allows clients to force serialization of the entire member list, a DoS/abuse surface (P3)

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, `limit` is taken directly from `params[:limit]` (`limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i`) and used in `group.users...limit(limit)` with no upper bound/clamp. A client can request an arbitrarily large `limit`, causing very large queries and serialization work on this public (non-admin) endpoint (`/groups/:group_id/members`), creating a plausible DoS/abuse surface.

adjudication_records.issue_text: findMembers in group.js returns undefined (not a promise) for empty name without offset normalization; callers like next/previous don't guard, and future callers chaining .then will throw (P3)
matched_golden_ids: Expected to return a value at the end of function - code paths without explicit returns will return undefined
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate points out that `findMembers` can return `undefined` for certain inputs (e.g., empty name), implying a code path without an explicit return (and thus not returning the expected value/promise). This aligns with the golden issue about missing returns leading to `undefined`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Controller `remove_member` uses `group.users.delete(user_id)` which skips `GroupUser` destroy callbacks, so `group.user_count` is not decremented; test only asserts raw `group.users.count == 0` and should also assert `group.user_count == 0` after reload

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#remove_member`, the diff clearly uses `group.users.delete(user_id)` (not `destroy` on a join record), which in Rails commonly bypasses join-model destroy callbacks/counter-cache updates. However, the diff does not show the `Group`/`GroupUser` association definitions or any callbacks/counter caches, so the claim that `group.user_count` will be wrong is not directly verifiable from this PR alone. The related spec only asserts `group.users.count` and does not check `user_count`, but whether that’s a correctness bug depends on unseen model behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `update` test uses `id: 1` assuming group id 1 is an automatic group via undocumented fixture/seed dependency instead of explicitly `Fabricate(:group, automatic: true)`

adjudication.rationale: In `spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb` under `context ".update"`, the new test hard-codes `xhr :put, :update, id: 1` and then does `Group.find(1)` while asserting name changes are ignored for an automatic group. The diff does not fabricate or set up any group with `id == 1` (or ensure it’s automatic), so the test implicitly depends on an external/undocumented seed/fixture assumption. This is a concrete, diff-grounded test robustness issue rather than an application runtime defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Missing negative tests for `create` action: failure branch (`render_json_error group`) never exercised, no test for invalid/duplicate group name despite uniqueness/format validations

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new `Admin::GroupsController#create` implementation with an explicit failure branch (`else render_json_error group`), but the updated controller spec under `context ".create"` only tests the success path (stripping spaces and creating the group) and does not exercise the error branch. While the finding mentions uniqueness/format validations (not shown in this diff), it is still accurate that there is no negative test covering `create` failing (e.g., invalid/duplicate name) despite the newly introduced failure handling.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `add_members` tests missing coverage for non-existent usernames (old 'succeeds silently' contract dropped), usernames with whitespace around commas (no `strip` on split parts causing silent lookup failures), and empty `usernames` string

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces new membership mutation logic in `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, parsing `usernames` via `usernames.split(",")` without trimming (`User.find_by_username(username)`), and the updated specs only cover adding valid users and rejecting automatic groups. There is no test coverage for edge cases the new parsing/lookup logic implies: non-existent usernames are silently ignored (due to `if user = ...`), whitespace around comma-separated usernames could cause lookup failures (no `strip` per token), and an empty `usernames` string would still hit `group.save` and return success. This is a specific, diff-grounded testing gap around new behavior, not a purely stylistic request.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No test coverage for the rewritten public `members` endpoint: pagination (`limit`/`offset`) now applies to automatic groups (previously unrestricted) and response shape changed to `{members, meta: {total, limit, offset}}`, which the client depends on

adjudication.rationale: The diff rewrites the public `GroupsController#members` endpoint to always apply `limit`/`offset` and to return a new JSON shape `{ members: ..., meta: { total, limit, offset } }` (app/controllers/groups_controller.rb). The client was updated to iterate `{{#each m in members}}` (app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/group/members.hbs) and `Discourse.Group#findMembers` now expects `result.meta.*` and `result.members` (app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js). However, the only added/modified controller specs are for `Admin::GroupsController`; there is no corresponding test added/updated for the public `GroupsController#members` behavior or response contract. Note: the finding’s claim that pagination for automatic groups was previously “unrestricted” is inaccurate (it was previously limited for automatic groups), but the lack of tests for the new response shape/pagination behavior is still a concrete, diff-grounded review issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Removed incremental PATCH tests with no equivalent coverage: removing a non-member is untested, and routing wiring for `DELETE` `remove_member` (config/routes.rb `delete "members"`) is unverified since the automatic-guard test uses `xhr :put` instead of the DELETE verb

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the prior incremental PATCH coverage (e.g. deleting a non-member / non-existent user cases) from `spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb` and does not add equivalent tests for the new member-management endpoints. In the new `context ".remove_member"`, the automatic-group guard test calls `xhr :put, :remove_member, ...` even though routing was changed to `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"` in `config/routes.rb`, so it doesn't exercise/verify the DELETE wiring. Also, there is no new test for removing a non-member (previously covered by the PATCH incremental delete tests).

adjudication_records.issue_text: `remove_member` test doesn't verify the removed user's membership via the serialized members endpoint, missing the serializer path the admin UI consumes

adjudication.rationale: In `spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb`, the `.remove_member` success test only asserts `group.users.count.should == 0` after `xhr :delete, :remove_member` and never exercises the UI-consumed members fetch path (`Discourse.Group#findMembers` -> GET `/groups/:name/members.json` returning `{ members: serialize_data(...), meta: ... }` in `GroupsController#members`). Given the diff changes the members endpoint response shape and the admin UI reloads via `findMembers()`, adding an assertion against that serialized endpoint would provide coverage for the actual integration path, but the current omission is a test gap rather than a verifiable functional defect in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: totalPages computed as Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1 creates a phantom page when user_count is an exact multiple of limit; should use Math.ceil

adjudication.rationale: In `admin-group.js.es6`, `totalPages` is computed as `Math.floor(this.get("user_count") / this.get("limit")) + 1`. When `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit` (e.g., 100/50), this yields one extra page (3 instead of 2). This can let `next` advance `offset` to `user_count`, and `findMembers()` will request `offset == total`, producing an empty member list (phantom last page). Using `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)` would avoid the extra page.

adjudication_records.issue_text: group.users.delete(user_id) bypasses membership bookkeeping in group.remove, potentially leaving stale user_count / data drift

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#remove_member`, the diff changes member removal to `group.users.delete(user_id)` instead of using the previously existing higher-level API (`group.remove(user)` was used in the removed `update_patch`). This is a concrete, diff-grounded concern because it bypasses any logic/callbacks/side effects encapsulated in `Group#remove` (bookkeeping, counters, etc.). However, the claim about leaving `user_count` stale/data drift can’t be verified from the diff alone because the implementation of `Group#remove`/counter maintenance isn’t shown here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: add_members silently ignores nonexistent usernames with no error or partial-failure reporting; should return a warning list or render_json_error

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, usernames are split and looked up with `User.find_by_username(username)`; if not found, the code simply skips them (`if user = ...; group.add(user); end`) and still returns `success_json` if `group.save` succeeds. This provides no feedback about invalid usernames. However, the previous incremental add logic (`update_patch`) also silently ignored non-existent users, so this is more of a product/UX/API design concern than a verifiable correctness defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: params.require(:usernames).split raises NoMethodError (500) if usernames is sent as an array; guard with Array(usernames).join(',')

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, the diff sets `usernames = params.require(:usernames)` and then unconditionally calls `usernames.split(",")`. If `usernames` is submitted as an Array (e.g. `usernames[]=a&usernames[]=b`), `split` will raise `NoMethodError`, producing a 500. The code has no normalization/guard (e.g. `Array(usernames).join(",")` or `usernames.to_s`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: addMembers never clears the usernames input (re-adds users on double click) and does not handle the promise from model.addMembers, so failures like 422 give no error message

adjudication.rationale: In `admin-group.js.es6`, the `addMembers` action explicitly notes `// TODO: should clear the input` and indeed never clears `this.get("usernames")` after calling `model.addMembers(...)`, so the same usernames can be submitted again (e.g., repeated clicks). Also, it does not `return` or otherwise handle the promise from `this.get("model").addMembers(...)`, so any rejection (e.g. 422 from `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`) is not handled locally in this action. The diff does not show any UI feedback/error handling tied to this action.

adjudication_records.issue_text: setupController fires findMembers() without returning/awaiting the promise, causing late-loading member list and transient 0/0 pagination computed against stale user_count: 0

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the prior `afterModel` hook that awaited `model.findMembers()` and instead calls `model.findMembers();` in `setupController` without returning the promise (see `admin_group_route.js` and `discourse/routes/group-members.js.es6`). Meanwhile `Discourse.Group` now initializes `user_count: 0` and pagination computed props in `admin-group.js.es6` return `0` pages when `user_count == 0`. In `admin/templates/group.hbs`, the pagination UI (`{{currentPage}}/{{totalPages}}`) is rendered for existing groups (`{{#if id}}`), so it will transiently show `0/0` until the async `findMembers()` completes and updates `user_count`/`members`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Pagination offset-clamping logic duplicated in three places (findMembers, next, previous), risking drift when clamp rules change

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows offset boundary logic implemented separately in multiple places: `Discourse.Group.findMembers` clamps `offset` via `Math.min(user_count, Math.max(offset, 0))`, while the admin controller actions `next` and `previous` each compute offsets with their own `Math.min(...)`/`Math.max(...)` formulas before calling `findMembers()`. This is real duplication that could drift if the pagination/clamping rules change, but it does not by itself create a verifiable broken behavior in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: removeMember/addMembers reload doesn't guard offset against shrunk lists, briefly showing an empty page after removing the last member of the final page

adjudication.rationale: In `Discourse.Group#removeMember` / `addMembers`, the success handler calls `self.findMembers()` without adjusting pagination. `findMembers` clamps the request offset using the *current* `this.get("user_count")` (which may be stale immediately after a removal): `offset = Math.min(this.get("user_count"), ...)`. If you remove the last member on the final page, the stored `user_count` can still reflect the old total, so it can request an offset that is now >= new total. The server then returns an empty `members` array (and `meta.offset` echoes the requested offset), and the model sets `members` to empty without any follow-up correction/refetch, producing a transient empty page. This behavior is directly implied by the diff in `group.js` and the reload calls in `removeMember`/`addMembers`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Dead show action in Admin::GroupsController (render nothing: true) predates the PR

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `Admin::GroupsController#show` still exists and still does `render nothing: true`, but this PR neither changes nor references that action. The finding’s key claim (“predates the PR”) cannot be verified from the diff alone, and no new defect/issue is introduced or exposed here related to `show`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Test in remove_member context uses xhr :put against a DELETE route, which would 404 in a real request path (test-only)

adjudication.rationale: In `spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb` under `context ".remove_member"`, the first test calls `xhr :put, :remove_member, group_id: 1, user_id: 42`, but the route added in `config/routes.rb` maps `remove_member` to `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"` (DELETE), not PUT. Controller specs can still hit the action directly, so it may pass, but it doesn't exercise the real HTTP verb/route combination and could hide routing/verb issues.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Test issues PUT to :remove_member instead of DELETE, so it routes to add_members and never verifies remove_member's automatic-group guard (silent-pass)

adjudication.rationale: In the new controller spec, the "cannot remove members from automatic groups" example calls `xhr :put, :remove_member, ...` even though the routes map `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"` and `put "members" => "groups#add_members"` (config/routes.rb). However, in a controller spec `:remove_member` is invoked directly, so it does not actually "route to add_members"; the automatic-group guard in `Admin::GroupsController#remove_member` would still run. The real issue is the test not using the correct HTTP verb / not exercising the real route mapping.

adjudication_records.issue_text: add_members silently skips non-existent usernames and returns success_json, with no error for typos

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, the code iterates `usernames.split(",")` and only adds users when `User.find_by_username(username)` returns a user; non-existent usernames are simply ignored, and the action still renders `success_json` if `group.save` succeeds. This matches the finding. However, the diff also shows prior behavior explicitly tested as “succeeds silently when adding non-existent users” (now removed along with the PATCH-based update flow), suggesting this may be intentional behavior/UX rather than a clear defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: add_members doesn't .strip split username items, so 'bob, alice' silently drops ' alice'

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::GroupsController#add_members, the code does `usernames.split(",").each do |username|` and then `User.find_by_username(username)` without trimming whitespace. If the input is comma+space separated (e.g. "bob, alice"), the second token will be " alice" and lookup will fail, so that user is silently not added.

adjudication_records.issue_text: remove_member calls group.users.delete before group.save, so a failed save returns 422 while the membership is already permanently removed

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#remove_member`, the code does `group.users.delete(user_id)` and only afterwards checks `if group.save` to decide whether to return success vs `422` (render_json_error). `group.users.delete` removes the join record immediately; it is not contingent on `group.save` and is not wrapped in a transaction here. So if `group.save` were to fail for any reason, the response would be a 422 even though the membership has already been removed, matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Removing a non-member silently succeeds with success_json, indistinguishable from an actual removal

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#remove_member`, the code unconditionally does `group.users.delete(user_id)` and then returns `success_json` as long as `group.save` succeeds (which it generally will even if nothing changed). There is no check that the user was actually a member, so a no-op removal is indistinguishable from a real removal. However, this is not clearly a defect in itself (DELETE endpoints are often intentionally idempotent), and the prior spec suite even explicitly allowed “succeeds silently when removing non-members,” suggesting this may be acceptable behavior rather than a bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: totalPages uses Math.floor(user_count/limit)+1, producing an extra empty navigable page when user_count is an exact multiple of limit; should be Math.ceil

adjudication.rationale: In `admin-group.js.es6`, `totalPages` is computed as `Math.floor(this.get("user_count") / this.get("limit")) + 1`. When `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit` (e.g., 100/50), this returns 3 instead of 2, enabling navigation to an extra page. The `next` action can then set `offset` to `user_count` (e.g., 100), and `findMembers()` will request `offset=100`, yielding an empty members list while `currentPage` becomes 3 (`Math.floor(100/50)+1`). Using `Math.ceil(user_count/limit)` (with proper zero handling) would avoid the empty page.

adjudication_records.issue_text: findMembers changed to bare 'return ;' (undefined) instead of resolving an empty array, breaking callers chaining .then on empty name

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js`, `findMembers` now does `if (Em.isEmpty(this.get('name'))) { return ; }`, whereas it previously returned `Ember.RSVP.resolve([])`. This changes the method from always returning a promise to sometimes returning `undefined`, which is an API/contract regression and could break any caller that expects a thenable (the finding’s scenario), although no `.then(...)` caller remains in the shown diff after the route changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: findMembers doesn't handle ajax errors, leaving stale members data silently displayed

adjudication.rationale: In the updated `Discourse.Group#findMembers` (app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js), the AJAX call only updates `members` inside `.then(...)` via `self.setProperties(...)` and has no error handling (`catch`/failure callback) and does not clear `members` before requesting. Routes/controllers now call `model.findMembers()` without awaiting or handling rejections (e.g., admin_group_route.js `setupController`, group-members route `setupController`, and pagination actions `next/previous`). If the request fails, the promise rejects silently at the call site and the previously-loaded `model.members` remains displayed, i.e., stale member data can remain visible with no feedback.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Race conditions in pagination and add/remove reloads: optimistic offset updates with no request sequencing or cancellation can show stale/overlapping pages

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces paginated member loading via `Group#findMembers`, which unconditionally `setProperties({ user_count, limit, offset, members })` from the AJAX response. In the controller, `next`/`previous` optimistically update `group.offset` and immediately call `group.findMembers()` with no request sequencing/cancellation. If a user triggers multiple `findMembers()` calls quickly (paging, or add/remove which also calls `findMembers()` in `.then()`), responses can arrive out of order and a slower earlier response will overwrite `members`/`offset` with stale data (since `findMembers` applies response meta regardless of current state). This can show the wrong page/members list.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Group name not URL-encoded in members request URL, breaking names with spaces or special characters

adjudication.rationale: The JS request does concatenate the group name directly into the path (e.g. `Discourse.ajax('/groups/' + this.get('name') + '/members.json', ...)`), but the diff also indicates group names are intended to follow the username rule and have “no spaces” (`name_placeholder: "Group name, no spaces, same as username rule"`). The diff does not show that group names with spaces or URL-breaking special characters are permitted/possible, so the claimed breakage for such names isn’t verifiable from this PR.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addMembers input never cleared after successful add, so re-clicking re-adds users with no visible feedback

adjudication.rationale: In `admin-group.js.es6` the `addMembers` action calls `this.get("model").addMembers(this.get("usernames"));` but never clears `usernames` afterward; the code even notes `// TODO: should clear the input`. This can lead to repeated submissions of the same usernames on subsequent clicks and provides no UI reset/feedback in the controller/template logic shown, but it’s primarily a UX/completeness issue rather than a strictly verifiable correctness failure from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Breaking removal of GET /admin/groups/users route with no deprecation or alias, breaking external consumers

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes a previously defined admin groups route: in `config/routes.rb` the line `get "users"` under `namespace :admin` / `resources :groups` is deleted and replaced with `delete "members"` and `put "members"`. There is no alias/redirect kept for the old `users` endpoint, so any client depending on that GET route would break. The finding’s exact path (`/admin/groups/users` vs likely `/admin/groups/:group_id/users`) is slightly imprecise, but the breaking removal of a GET `users` route is verifiable in the diff.
